outgoing.name: England
outgoing.excerpt: Edmond Halley FRS (sometimes "Edmund", November 8, 1656 – January 14, 1742) was an English astronomer, geophysicist, mathematician, meteorologist, and physicist.

outgoing.name: Geometry
outgoing.excerpt: In November 1703 he was appointed Savilian professor of geometry at Oxford University, and received an honorary degree of doctor of laws in 1710.

outgoing.name: Gravitation
outgoing.excerpt: He spent most of his time on lunar observations, but was also interested in the problems of gravity.

outgoing.name: London
outgoing.excerpt: Halley was born at Haggerston, London, the son of a wealthy soapboiler.

outgoing.name: Magnetism
outgoing.excerpt: In 1698 he received a commission as captain of HMS Paramore to make extensive observations on the conditions of terrestrial magnetism.

outgoing.name: River Thames
outgoing.excerpt: In a demonstration, Halley and five companions dived to 60 feet in the River Thames, and remained there for over one and a half hours.

outgoing.name: Solar System

outgoing.name: Transit of Venus
